standard.title: Compare fractions with related denominators
standard.description: Compare and order fractions with the same and related denominators including mixed numerals, applying knowledge of factors and multiples; represent these fractions on a number line
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can represent fractions as parts of a whole and on a number line, and identify equivalences (AC9M4N03, AC9M4N04). They have not yet compared fractions with related (not same) denominators, or worked with mixed numerals systematically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students compare and order fractions with the same and related denominators including mixed numerals, applying knowledge of factors and multiples, and represent these on a number line.

nodes.label: Equivalent fractions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can generate equivalent fractions by multiplying or dividing numerator and denominator by the same factor.
nodes.minimum_width: Generate at least 3 equivalent fractions for a given fraction using multiplication or division; explain why they are equivalent.
nodes.typical_width: Use factor knowledge to find equivalent fractions systematically; represent equivalences on fraction walls and number lines; simplify fractions using common factors.
wider: Connect equivalent fractions to percentage and decimal representations
Use area models to justify equivalence visually

response_modes.reason: Fluency with equivalence generation is the prerequisite skill for all comparison and addition of fractions. Students need it to be automatic before comparison tasks become tractable.

nodes.hinge_reason: Equivalent fraction generation is directly required by Node 2 — students who cannot convert between equivalent forms cannot identify related denominators or make the conversion needed to compare fractions.
success_criteria: Student generates equivalent fractions correctly using multiplication and division
Student explains why two fractions are equivalent using numerator-denominator reasoning

nodes.label: Related denominators
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify when denominators are related (one is a multiple of the other) and use this to compare fractions.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify whether two fractions have related denominators; convert the smaller denominator to the larger using factor knowledge to enable comparison.
nodes.typical_width: Compare fractions with related denominators across a range of examples; apply multiples knowledge to determine the conversion factor; verify using number lines.
wider: Investigate what happens when denominators share a common factor but neither is a multiple of the other
Connect to LCM: what is the smallest denominator both fractions can share?

response_modes.reason: Students commonly try to compare numerators or denominators independently without converting. Varied fraction pairs — including non-obvious related pairs — expose the limitation of shortcut strategies.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: LCM connections give advancing students a bridge to the general comparison method used in Year 6.
success_criteria: Student identifies whether two fractions have related denominators
Student correctly converts to a common denominator and compares

nodes.label: Mixed numerals
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can represent, compare and order mixed numerals on a number line.
nodes.minimum_width: Represent a mixed numeral on a number line; compare two mixed numerals with the same denominator.
nodes.typical_width: Convert between improper fractions and mixed numerals; compare mixed numerals with related denominators; order sets of mixed numerals and fractions on a number line.
wider: Use measurement contexts (e.g. lengths in metres and fractions of metres) to give mixed numerals meaning
Investigate Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander uses of fractional and proportional quantities in cultural contexts
success_criteria: Student places mixed numerals on a number line at correct positions
Student compares two mixed numerals using equivalence reasoning

nodes.label: Ordering fractions with factors and multiples
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can order a mixed set of fractions including mixed numerals with related denominators by applying factor and multiple knowledge.
nodes.minimum_width: Order a set of 4+ fractions (including at least one mixed numeral) with related denominators, showing the common denominator used.
nodes.typical_width: Order mixed sets of fractions across a variety of related denominators; represent the ordered set on a number line; explain the reasoning chain.
wider: Design fraction ordering puzzles that require multi-step factor reasoning
Connect fraction ordering to proportional reasoning: which fraction of a quantity is larger?

response_modes.reason: This node is where equivalence, related denominators, mixed numerals and factor knowledge all operate together. Coordination of these components is the learning, not any single component in isolation.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-step reasoning with creative contexts (puzzles, proportional comparison) is rich territory for advancing students.
success_criteria: Student orders a set of fractions with related denominators correctly, showing working
Student represents the ordered set accurately on a number line
